subject: microbiology
title: Intestinal Coccidia, Balantidium coli and Trichomonas vaginalis

steps.tx: The foodborne coccidian **Cyclospora cayetanensis** causes prolonged, relapsing, watery diarrhoea associated with foreign travel or consuming imported contaminated produce such as raspberries and basil. Freshly excreted fecal oocysts are unsporulated and non-infectious, requiring one to two weeks in warm soil to mature into infective double-walled cysts, precluding direct person-to-person transmission.
steps.say: Contaminated berries transmit unsporulated Cyclospora oocysts that require environmental soil maturation.

vis.caption: Morphologic spectrum of intestinal coccidia, Balantidium coli, and Trichomonas [Credit: CDC, StewardMD cleared]

steps.tx: On fecal microscopy stained with modified Ziehl-Neelsen, Cyclospora appears as spherical oocysts measuring eight to ten micrometres in diameter, exactly twice the diameter of Cryptosporidium. They display variable acid-fastness, ranging from dark magenta to unstained glassy **ghost oocysts**. Crucially, under epifluorescence microscopy with ultraviolet illumination at three hundred and sixty-five nanometres, they exhibit bright neon-blue autofluorescence.
steps.say: Eight to ten micrometre oocysts exhibit variable acid-fast staining and vivid neon blue ultraviolet autofluorescence.

left.title: Cyclospora cayetanensis
points: Variable acid fastness with pale ghost forms
Neon blue autofluorescence under 365 nm UV

right.title: Cystoisospora belli
points: Bright green to yellow UV autofluorescence

steps.tx: Round oocysts on a modified Ziehl Neelsen stool smear take the dye unevenly, some deep magenta and some clear. The clear forms are the **ghost oocysts** of Cyclospora cayetanensis. Each measures about 8 to 10 micrometres, twice the diameter of Cryptosporidium. Under ultraviolet light at 365 nanometres they autofluoresce a bright neon blue. Variable acid fast staining plus that blue glow separates them from similar coccidia in the same stool.
steps.say: Cyclospora oocysts are about 8 to 10 micrometres wide, twice Cryptosporidium, and they stain from deep pink to colourless ghosts. Under ultraviolet light they glow neon blue, which confirms the identification.

vis.alt: Modified Ziehl Neelsen stain of stool shows round Cyclospora oocysts, some acid fast and some unstained ghost forms.
vis.caption: Spherical oocysts take the acid fast stain unevenly, so magenta forms lie beside pale ghost forms of similar size. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: The large coccidian **Cystoisospora belli**, historically called Isospora belli, is an opportunistic cause of profuse watery diarrhoea and malabsorption in immunocompromised patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome. Fecal wet preparations demonstrate massive, elongated, spindle-shaped or ellipsoidal oocysts measuring twenty to thirty-three micrometres, each containing a single central granular sporoblast.
steps.say: Large spindle-shaped Cystoisospora oocysts cause severe chronic malabsorptive diarrhoea in HIV infection.

rows: Found in muscular sarcocysts or stool

steps.tx: A unique haematological hallmark that distinguishes Cystoisospora from other intestinal protozoal pathogens is prominent **peripheral blood eosinophilia**. Most protozoal enteritides run their course without eliciting systemic allergic or eosinophilic responses. In cystoisosporiasis, tissue invasion of the lamina propria stimulates interleukin-5 release, prompting eosinophil counts to exceed fifteen percent of total leukocytes.
steps.say: Intestinal mucosal invasion triggers interleukin five release, causing prominent peripheral blood eosinophilia.

nodes.label: Ingested Cystoisospora oocyst invades jejunal lamina propria
Intense mucosal inflammation triggers T-cell interleukin-5 secretion
Bone marrow releases eosinophils, generating diagnostic peripheral eosinophilia

steps.tx: The treatment of choice for both Cyclospora cayetanensis and Cystoisospora belli is oral **trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole**, which provides rapid microbiological clearance and resolution of diarrhoea. In patients with human immunodeficiency virus, chronic secondary prophylaxis with cotrimoxazole is necessary to prevent frequent post-treatment relapses. For sulpha-allergic individuals, oral ciprofloxacin serves as a secondary alternative.
steps.say: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is curative for both Cyclospora and Cystoisospora, with ciprofloxacin as alternative.

rows: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS twice daily for 7 days
Cotrimoxazole three times weekly if HIV positive
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole DS four times daily for 10 days

steps.tx: The giant ciliated protozoan **Balantidium coli** is the largest protozoan and the only ciliate known to infect humans. Pigs serve as the principal natural reservoir, and infection spreads through ingestion of porcine fecal cysts. Trophozoites measure fifty to one hundred micrometres, display rapid rotary tumbling motility driven by cilia, and harbor a prominent kidney-shaped macronucleus alongside a contractile vacuole.
steps.say: Swine handlers risk infection by giant ciliated Balantidium, recognizable by its kidney-shaped macronucleus.

left.title: Balantidium coli trophozoite
points: Covered uniformly with rows of motile cilia
Secretes hyaluronidase to invade colonic submucosa

right.title: Clinical manifestations
points: Deep mucosal ulcerations with ragged edges
Tetracycline is the therapeutic drug of choice

steps.tx: The sexually transmitted flagellate **Trichomonas vaginalis** exists exclusively as a motile trophozoite, lacking any cyst stage in its life cycle. The pear-shaped organism possesses four anterior flagella and an undulating membrane extending half the length of the cell, generating characteristic rapid jerky, twitching motility on immediate saline wet mount examination of vaginal secretions.
steps.say: Trichomonas lacks a cyst stage, moving with jerky twitching motility powered by four flagella.

rows: Trophozoite only; no cyst stage exists
Jerky, non-directional twitching motility on saline mount
Profuse, frothy, thin, greenish-yellow with foul odour
Elevated markedly above 4.5, typically between 5.0 and 6.0

steps.tx: Patients present with a profuse, malodorous, frothy, greenish-yellow vaginal discharge accompanied by severe pruritus and dysuria. Colposcopic examination reveals punctate mucosal haemorrhages over the cervix and upper vagina, termed the **strawberry cervix** or colpitis macularis. Treatment requires single-dose oral metronidazole or tinidazole, and treating sexual partners simultaneously is mandatory to avoid ping-pong reinfection.
steps.say: Punctate cervical petechiae create a strawberry cervix; both sexual partners must receive metronidazole.

nodes.label: Identify frothy greenish-yellow discharge and elevated vaginal pH over 4.5
Demonstrate motile trichomonads on immediate normal saline wet mount
Administer single 2g oral metronidazole to both index patient and sexual partner
